note.label: The Waters of Noah Will Be Fire

precepts.why:
“For a small moment have I forsaken thee; but with great mercies will I gather thee.” When you ponder on that, for a small moment have I forsaken thee, it seems like forever and ever to you and me. But to the Lord it is only a small moment. Only a small moment.

Peter shows why: “But, beloved, be not ignorant of this one thing, that one day is with the Lord as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day.” One day with the Lord is as a thousand years. So to us it has been thousands of years of being forsaken, but the Lord says, listen, it is only a small moment. It has been one day in the Lord’s time.

note.label: Drowning in Sin & Perdition

precepts.why:
Peter says “there shall come in the last days scoffers, walking after their own lusts, And saying, Where is the promise of his coming?” A scoffer mocks and ridicules; he doesn't just disagree, he expresses insolent doubt and derision, openly opposing God and divine truth, arrogant, close-minded and fueled by pride. Of all the reasons people scoff at the Bible, one stands out: the problem of evil and suffering, why God would permit harm.

An ex-pastor turned atheist, who preached in the streets and the prisons for fifteen years, now says the Bible is fiction, that black people are not Israelites, that even if we were he would hate that God, and asks what Jesus did about slavery, Jim Crow and the Trail of Tears. Going through his page, the reason showed itself: he has a child in remission from stage four brain cancer. That's a lot of trauma. Maybe they tried the holy water and the laying on of hands and nothing worked.

A lot of times when bad things happen, people turn around and blame God: God, why did you do this to me? That is why a lot of people turn atheist. One sister had a miscarriage and started blaming God. But we have to do what Job did. Job lost his children, his wealth and his health, and “In all this Job sinned not, nor charged God foolishly.” He didn't charge God foolishly. That's it. We cannot charge God foolishly, knowing that he has his reasons.

And as for the cures for cancer being hidden: after the Epstein files dropped we saw how much the pharmaceutical companies were holding back. They already have patents on things and hold them back because there is more money in the treatment than the cure. The scoffer blames God for what the wicked have done, and he is willingly ignorant, like the scoffers in the days of Noah, whom God put to death.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
“And God did rest the seventh day from all his works.” Peter shows how that seventh day reaches forward to the kingdom: “But the heavens and the earth, which are now, by the same word are kept in store, reserved unto fire against the day of judgment and perdition of ungodly men. But, beloved, be not ignorant of this one thing, that one day is with the Lord as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day.”

One day with the Lord, brothers, is a thousand years. So the seventh day is not only the Sabbath we keep each week; it maps to a thousand years, the reign that comes after the heavens and earth that are now are reserved unto fire against the day of judgment.

That is why “There remaineth therefore a rest to the people of God.” The rest of the seventh day is the similitude, and the thousand years is the substance: the day we reign with Christ, as Revelation 20:4 shows.

note.label: The Mercy and Humility of King Manasseh

precepts.why:
Manasseh prays, “Be not angry with me for ever, by reserving evil for me; neither condemn me to the lower parts of the earth.” Peter shows the great evil reserved at the end: “But the heavens and the earth, which are now, by the same word are kept in store, reserved unto fire against the day of judgment and perdition of ungodly men.”

The heavens and the earth are reserved unto fire: nuclear fire, and the hellfire that follows after it. That is what the ungodly are reserved for, and that is what Manasseh was asking not to be reserved for him. The lower parts of the earth he speaks of go into the hellfire again.

Then he says, “For thou art the God, even the God of them that repent.” He is the God of them that repent. Unto them that repent he grants return. So humble yourself before you are sick, examine yourself before judgment, and in the time of sins show repentance, because the fire is already reserved for the ungodly.

note.label: The Beauty And The Beast

precepts.why:
Zephaniah speaks of the decree; Peter shows it will not fail: “The Lord is not slack concerning his promise, as some men count slackness”. What the Lord said is exactly what will come to pass. He “is longsuffering to us-ward, not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance.” The Lord does not want any of his people to perish, and that is why he is giving us time to get ourselves right. That does not mean he will not put the wicked to death.

“But the day of the Lord will come as a thief in the night”, whether you get yourself right or not, “in the which the heavens shall pass away with a great noise, and the elements shall melt with fervent heat”. How is that possible? By nuclear fire: the same burning with fire the ten horns bring on the whore.

“Seeing then that all these things shall be dissolved, what manner of persons ought ye to be”? That goes to Deacon Yashua’s point. Should we sit with the popcorn just watching? Eating popcorn is not a sin, with a little butter and salt. But if that is all you are doing and you are not applying, that is when it becomes an issue.

This is not the time to kick our feet up or bug out. Now is the time to work like we never worked before and to increase in righteousness.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walking Through Galatians

precepts.why:
Peter says Paul wrote “according to the wisdom given unto him”, and wisdom is not a what but a who: Christ is the wisdom given to Paul. And Peter read “all his epistles”. He didn't say, this is off but I'll let it slide. If Paul wrote things that were off, that implicates Peter; if it implicates Peter it implicates James; and it implicates John, the last surviving disciple, who never wrote against Paul. You make Christ a negligent Messiah who sat quiet while Paul wrote error and then waited three thousand years to send somebody to fix it.

So what did Paul write from? “Having therefore obtained help of God, I continue unto this day, witnessing both to small and great, saying none other things than those which the prophets and Moses did say should come”. When Paul crafted his letters, his primary reference was none other than what the prophets and Moses wrote. That is Paul's source material.

That is why Peter says the unlearned and unstable wrest Paul “as they do also the other scriptures”: the law and the prophets. Wrest is short for wrestle; they twist Paul into saying what he did not say, because they don't really believe what the Bible says. The error of the wicked takes Paul's letters and says all nations can be saved, Paul grafted the nations in, we can commit adultery, the Sabbath is changed, we don't have to keep the laws anymore. Don't fall from your own stedfastness: Paul said none other things than Moses and the prophets.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walking Through Galatians

precepts.why:
When they appointed Paul a day, many came to his lodging, “to whom he expounded and testified the kingdom of God, persuading them concerning Jesus, both out of the law of Moses, and out of the prophets, from morning till evening.” That is the other scriptures. His source material was the Old Testament.

Write this down: Paul's letters predate the gospels, with the exception of Mark. Mark, Luke and Matthew are the synoptic gospels, and it is said Matthew and Luke borrowed from Mark, because Mark was Peter's scribe. That is why Peter has no gospel: Mark is Peter's gospel, and it makes sense that it is the oldest, since Peter's and Paul's ministries were at the same time. Paul's letters range from the forties to the sixties AD. John was written around 90 AD, twenty years after Rome besieged Jerusalem in 70 AD, and Revelation around 95 to 100 AD.

So Paul was not pulling from John 3:16, because when he wrote his letters there was no John 3:16. He was not quoting John, Matthew or Luke; his letters came before them. Luke was travelling with him, and Luke wrote both Luke and Acts: Acts is basically a second Luke, Luke's letter number two.

That is why you cannot understand Paul's letters, the things hard to be understood, without the law and the prophets. Paul persuaded men concerning Jesus out of Moses and the prophets from morning till evening, and the unlearned who don't know those scriptures wrest Paul unto their own destruction.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walk Through of Romans 5

precepts.why:
Peter says “our beloved brother Paul also according to the wisdom given unto him hath written unto you”. Peter is giving kudos and respect to Paul for the wisdom that was in him, and that wisdom is Christ, the spirit of Christ. But in Paul's epistles “are some things hard to be understood, which they that are unlearned and unstable wrest”. So first get clear on who Paul was writing to.

“To all that be in Rome, beloved of God, called to be saints: Grace to you and peace from God our Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ.” Called to be saints. Who are the saints? Psalms 148 speaks of “the praise of all his saints; even of the children of Israel, a people near unto him.” The children of Israel are the saints. We are the saints.

Some Christians say Paul was writing to Israelites and other nations at the same time. No. That is not who the letter is addressed to. It is addressed to the saints at Rome. Other nations are never referred to as saints. When you twist that and teach that your oppressor can be granted the same benefits as you, that the nations receive some twisted salvation, you have been “led away with the error of the wicked” and fallen from your own stedfastness. It is a whole different gospel, and that is how the unlearned wrest Paul unto their own destruction.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walk Through of Romans 5

precepts.why:
Get some clarity on who Paul is writing to: “Behold, thou art called a Jew, and restest in the law, and makest thy boast of God”. Paul is writing to the Jews. There is obviously northern kingdom in the congregations too, but he is writing to Judah.

Romans 7 says the same: “Know ye not, brethren, (for I speak to them that know the law,)”. Why does he speak to them that know the law? Because he is writing to Jews, “how that the law hath dominion over a man as long as he liveth”.

So Paul is writing to Jews, to those who know the law, to the saints at Rome. Is he addressing both Jews and Gentiles in the church? Yes, but the Gentiles there are the northern kingdom, and they are all saints. He is not writing to other nations at all.

That is why Peter says the unlearned wrest Paul “as they do also the other scriptures”. They stumble because they think Paul was writing things out of thin air to all nations, when he was writing to Israel, men who rested in the law and boasted of God. Know who the letter is addressed to and much of what is hard to be understood in Paul becomes plain.

precepts.why:

Paul only taught what Moses and the prophets said.

And in Acts 28, when many came to his lodging, he “expounded and testified the kingdom of God, persuading them concerning Jesus, both out of the law of Moses, and out of the prophets, from morning till evening.” His letters are based on the law and the prophets. He was not sitting around making things up.

That is why Peter mentions “the other scriptures”: to understand Paul's letters you must understand the other scriptures. Are there places where the spirit of Christ spoke through Paul and things were added? Yes. Paul's letters are 99.9 percent law and prophets, and maybe one percent is something like the unbelieving wife departing, which is not found in Moses, because under Moses, if she did not believe, she got death. Your wife could believe in Satan in the wilderness and she got death. That was added for that time, and that is “the wisdom given unto him”: Christ speaking through Paul.

When people don't study Paul, they say Paul's letters aren't authoritative, Mark and Luke weren't of the twelve, and they begin to speak evil of dignities. Then the Lord blinds their minds, and Satan has them teaching that nations can be saved. We have been thoroughbreds in Paul's letters since learning Acts 10 and Romans 11 at the Bishop's house in 2006.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart

precepts.why:
Peter says “that one day is with the Lord as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day.” David says our days are seventy, eighty years. Do the math: if a thousand years is one day to God, eighty years is 0.08 of a day, about an hour and fifty-five minutes. An entire human lifetime is less than two hours to God, and it may be even less than that; the concept of time does not apply to the Ancient of days. Eighty years and you come back and God says, you just left, why you back already?

That is why the scriptures say things like Baruch: “My children, suffer patiently the wrath that is come upon you from God: for thine enemy hath persecuted thee”. It is happening right now. We are going through it, and it seems like forever, because down here it takes forever to become an adult, to get your license, to turn 21. Lord, come save us; they are doing their worst.

Then, “but shortly thou shalt see his destruction, and shalt tread upon his neck.” Shortly: in less than a few minutes of God's time your life is over, and in an hour or so you see the destruction of your enemy and have a lifetime of God time, eternal. So suffer patiently. What seems long to us is short to him.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart

precepts.why:
“For a small moment have I forsaken thee; but with great mercies will I gather thee.” A small moment. That is why God says small moment: it is not even two hours to him, not even a day to him. If a thousand years is as one day with the Lord, our whole captivity is a moment in his eyes.

“In a little wrath I hid my face from thee for a moment; but with everlasting kindness will I have mercy on thee, saith the Lord thy Redeemer.” For a moment. Start thinking like that: I'm only here for a short while.

And since it is only a moment, Peter gives the wisdom Christ put in his mouth: “Humble yourselves therefore under the mighty hand of God, that he may exalt you in due time”. The real exaltation we want is when we go back to him: a crown from God Almighty, and you can't get any higher than that. “Casting all your care upon him; for he careth for you.” He knows you only have a short amount of time here.

Then, “for God proved them, and found them worthy for himself.” The chastising is the proving. He tries us to find us worthy unto himself. So we have to endure to the end, people.
